variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Adapted: Variables begin with an uppercase letter or underscore.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Adapted: Prolog types include atoms, numbers, variables, and compound terms.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
Result is A + B.
X =:= Y. % Arithmetic equality
A = B. % Unification
operators.notes: Prolog uses 'is' for arithmetic evaluation and = for unification.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
check_score(Score, Grade) :-
    ( Score >= 90 -> Grade = 'A'
    ; Score >= 80 -> Grade = 'B'
    ; Grade = 'C'
    ).

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: Adapted: Prolog uses recursion over lists instead of for loops.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
loop(0).
loop(N) :-
    N > 0,
    do_something,
    Next is N - 1,
    loop(Next).
while_loop.notes: Adapted: Tail recursion serves as a while loop.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
add_numbers(A, B, Result) :-
    Result is A + B.
functions.notes: Adapted: Functions are predicates where the last argument is usually the output.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.notes: Adapted: Lists are used instead of traditional arrays.

maps.title: Maps
maps.notes: Adapted: Association lists (key-value pairs) are used as maps.

comments.title: Comments
comments.code:
-- Single-line comment in Prolog
/* Multi-line comment */
comments.notes: Prolog uses -- for line comments and /* */ for blocks.

numbers.title: Numbers & Decimal Data
numbers.notes: Prolog represents exact decimal precisions alongside standard integer types.

booleans.title: Booleans & Predicates
booleans.code:
-- Three-valued logic (TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN)
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND deleted_at IS NULL
booleans.notes: Prolog evaluates predicates using declarative boolean conditions with NULL semantics.

type_casting.title: Type Casting (CAST/CONVERT)
type_casting.notes: Prolog casts types using CAST(expr AS target_type) expressions.

strings.title: Strings & Text Literals
strings.code: SELECT 'String literal' AS col, N'Unicode text' AS unicode_col;
strings.notes: Prolog encloses character literals in single quotes with optional N prefix for Unicode.

string_formatting.title: String Concatenation
string_formatting.code: SELECT CONCAT('User: ', username, ' (', email, ')') FROM users;
string_formatting.notes: Prolog formats and joins textual columns using CONCAT or string concatenation operators.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching (LIKE & CASE)
pattern_matching.code:
SELECT CASE 
    WHEN score >= 90 THEN 'A'
    WHEN score >= 80 THEN 'B'
    ELSE 'C'
END AS grade
WHERE email LIKE '%@example.com';
pattern_matching.notes: Prolog performs conditional classification via CASE WHEN and pattern search with LIKE.

range.title: Ranges (BETWEEN & LIMIT/OFFSET)
range.notes: Prolog defines range intervals with BETWEEN and pagination ranges via LIMIT/OFFSET.

iterators.title: Cursors & Window Functions
iterators.notes: Prolog processes ordered sequences set-by-set using window functions or procedural cursors.

oop_classes.title: Schemas & Tables (Entities)
oop_classes.notes: Prolog structures entities through relational tables, constraints, and views.

lists.title: Tables & Arrays
lists.code:
-- Array or temporary result table
SELECT ARRAY[1, 2, 3] AS num_list;
lists.notes: Prolog supports array column types or relation rowsets representing lists.

tuples.title: Rows & Composite Types
tuples.notes: Prolog represents tuples as table rows or composite record types.

sets.title: Set Queries (UNION, INTERSECT)
sets.notes: Prolog combines dataset results using relational algebra (UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT).

modules_import.title: Schemas & Extensions
modules_import.code:
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "uuid-ossp";
SET search_path TO my_schema, public;
modules_import.notes: Prolog manages namespaces and modular capabilities through schemas and extensions.
